metrics.method: complete-slate user-centered BCE with learned global bias

method_selection.citation: gauge-fixing rationale (per-user constant shifts leave the metric invariant); pairwise-consistency literature.
method_selection.why: No usable learning curve supports an overfit or underfit diagnosis. The evaluator depends only on within-user ordering, while ordinary BCE spends capacity fitting per-user logit offsets that cannot affect GAUC/nDCG. User-centered BCE removes this nuisance while retaining the accepted package's BPR term and regularization. It is untried in this lineage, cheap, and previously delivered +0.0026, giving the best eligible chance of clearing the 0.002 convergence threshold, though gain on the stronger 0.6040 parent may be smaller.

rejected.reason: Eligible and cheap, but it is an untried extension of gauge fixing; the measured-win mean-centering version should be established first.
Metric-aligned but untried, and closely related delta-nDCG pair weighting was measured dead in multiple runs; expected gain is less credible than the replicated gauge-fixed BCE result.
Already present in the accepted parent package, so selecting it would repeat a champion component rather than test a new mechanism.
